subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What does it take to be active outside safely and repeatedly?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of weather, terrain, daylight, and clothing decisions in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe route planning and telling someone where you are going using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving trail, road, and shared-space etiquette; correct it and explain why.
Connect environmental care and leave-no-trace practice with finding free public activity spaces in a community and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Plan and complete one guardian-approved outdoor activity, including the safety plan, and produce a map of free activity spaces reachable from home.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Distance, duration, terrain, and pace are learner-set. An indoor or home-yard equivalent is available in full for any learner for whom outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
